Alpha Diversity Wrapper Function

Source: R/alpha_div.r
alpha_div.Rd

Alpha Diversity Wrapper Function

Usage

alpha_div(
  counts,
  metric,
  norm = "percent",
  cutoff = 10L,
  digits = 3L,
  tree = NULL,
  margin = 1L,
  q = 2,
  bias_corrected = TRUE,
  cpus = n_cpus()
)

Arguments

counts

A numeric matrix of count data (samples \(\times\) features). Typically contains absolute abundances (integer counts), though proportions are also accepted.

metric

The name of an alpha diversity metric. One of c('ace', 'berger', 'brillouin', 'chao1', 'dominance', 'faith', 'fisher', 'gini', 'goods_coverage', 'heip', 'hill', 'inv_simpson', 'margalef', 'mcintosh', 'mcintosh_evenness', 'menhinick', 'observed', 'pielou', 'renyi', 'shannon', 'simpson', 'simpson_evenness', 'squares', 'strong', 'tsallis'). Case-insensitive and partial name matching is supported, as are scikit-bio's names (such as 'pielou_e', 'simpson_d', 'observed_features' and 'enspie'). Programmatic access via list_metrics('alpha').

norm

Normalize the incoming counts. Options are:

  • 'none': No transformation.

  • 'percent': Relative abundance (sample abundances sum to 1).

  • 'hellinger': Square root of relative abundance (the Hellinger transformation).

  • 'binary': Unweighted presence/absence (each count is either 0 or 1).

  • 'clr': Centered log ratio.

  • 'rclr': Robust centered log ratio.

  • 'log': Log relative abundance (log-TSS), with pseudocount added to every value first.

  • 'chisq': The chi-square transformation, which uses the whole table's feature totals (see normalize()).

Default: 'none'.

cutoff

The maximum number of observations to consider "rare". Default: 10.

digits

Precision of the returned values, in number of decimal places. E.g. the default digits=3 could return 6.392.

tree

A phylo-class object representing the phylogenetic tree for the OTUs in counts. The OTU identifiers given by colnames(counts) must be present in tree. Can be omitted if a tree is embedded with the counts object or as attr(counts, 'tree').

margin

The margin containing samples. 1 if samples are rows, 2 if samples are columns. Ignored when counts is a special object class (e.g. phyloseq). Default: 1

q

The order of a Hill number, or of Rényi's or Tsallis's entropy: a single number of at least 0, where Inf is allowed. Only used by hill(), renyi() and tsallis(). Default: 2, as scikit-bio (which calls it order).

bias_corrected

For Chao1 only: use the bias-corrected form (the default, as scikit-bio and QIIME 2), or the classic form when a sample has both singletons and doubletons (FALSE). See chao1().

cpus

How many parallel processing threads should be used. The default, n_cpus(), is the CPU cores this R process may use, within any limits set on it. Results are the same for any cpus.

Value

A numeric vector, one value per sample, named by the samples. To compute several metrics, call alpha_div() once for each (see the examples).

Details

Integer Count Requirements

A frequent and critical error in alpha diversity analysis is providing the wrong type of data to a metric's formula. Some indices are mathematically defined based on counts of individuals and require raw, integer abundance data. Others are based on proportional abundances and can accept either integer counts (which are then converted to proportions) or pre-normalized proportional data. Using proportional data with a metric that requires integer counts will return an error message.

Requires Integer Counts Only

  • Chao1

  • ACE

  • Squares Richness Estimator

  • Margalef's Index

  • Menhinick's Index

  • Fisher's Alpha

  • Brillouin Index

  • McIntosh Index

  • McIntosh's Evenness

  • Good's Coverage

Can Use Proportional Data

  • Observed Features

  • Shannon Index

  • Gini-Simpson Index

  • Inverse Simpson Index

  • Hill Numbers, Rényi and Tsallis Entropies

  • Pielou's, Heip's and Simpson's Evenness

  • Berger-Parker Index

  • Simpson's and Strong's Dominance Indices

  • Gini Index

  • Faith's PD

Differences from scikit-bio

The metrics follow skbio.diversity.alpha (scikit-bio 0.7.4), which QIIME 2's diversity alpha runs, with these differences:

  • Logarithms are natural. scikit-bio's shannon(), pielou_e() and renyi() take a base; divide ecodive's shannon() and renyi() by log(base) instead. Pielou's evenness doesn't depend on the base.

  • No finite option for simpson(), dominance() and inv_simpson() (scikit-bio's estimator without replacement).

  • The gini() index is computed by rectangles only (scikit-bio's default method = "rectangles", not "trapezoids").

  • A sample with no observations is NA for every metric. scikit-bio gives nan for most metrics, but 0 for chao1() and gini_index().

  • chao1(bias_corrected = FALSE) is the classic formula, falling back on the bias-corrected one when a sample has no singletons or no doubletons, exactly as scikit-bio does.

Input Types

The counts parameter is designed to accept a simple numeric matrix, but seamlessly supports objects from the following biological data packages:

  • phyloseq

  • rbiom

  • SummarizedExperiment

  • TreeSummarizedExperiment

For large datasets, standard matrix operations may be slow. See vignette('performance') for details on using optimized formats (e.g. sparse matrices) and parallel processing.

Examples

    # Example counts matrix
    ex_counts
#>        Streptococcus Bacteroides Corynebacterium Haemophilus Propionibacterium
#> Saliva           162           2               0         180                 1
#> Gums             793           4               0          87                 1
#> Nose              22           2             498           2               251
#> Stool              1         611               1           1                 0
#>        Staphylococcus
#> Saliva              0
#> Gums                1
#> Nose              236
#> Stool               1
    
    # Shannon diversity values
    alpha_div(ex_counts, 'Shannon')
#>     Saliva       Gums       Nose      Stool 
#> 0.74119910 0.36684449 1.14222899 0.04824952 
    
    # Chao1 diversity values
    alpha_div(ex_counts, 'c')
#> Saliva   Gums   Nose  Stool 
#>      4      6      6     11 
    
    # Faith PD values
    alpha_div(ex_counts, 'faith', tree = ex_tree)
#> Saliva   Gums   Nose  Stool 
#>    180    191    215    202 
    
    # Hill number of order 1 (the exponential of Shannon's entropy)
    alpha_div(ex_counts, 'hill', q = 1)
#>   Saliva     Gums     Nose    Stool 
#> 2.098450 1.443173 3.133746 1.049432 
    
    # Several metrics: one call each
    sapply(c('observed', 'shannon', 'pielou'), alpha_div, counts = ex_counts)
#>        observed    shannon     pielou
#> Saliva        4 0.74119910 0.53466213
#> Gums          5 0.36684449 0.22793330
#> Nose          6 1.14222899 0.63749014
#> Stool         5 0.04824952 0.02997911
